_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. Anchors are in FITTED car space (auto-fit ~3.4 units long, grounded y=0, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left) — same frame as lib/systems.js. `materials` are GLB material-name substrings the frontend matches (first-match-wins in this part order — put specific parts before general ones); empty = not a mesh in this GLB, shown as an info callout. Non-modeled drivetrain/suspension with those exact ids render the procedural stand-in. The Z06 ships a REAL engine mesh (EngineA — the LT6) plus real wheels, brakes (calipers), interior, and lights; only the transaxle and suspension are procedural stand-ins. Copy grounded on data/cars/72-chevrolet-corvette-z06-c8.json (systems_map); anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs + the sibling .partmap.json.

parts.label: LT6 5.5L Flat-Plane V8
parts.summary: The LT6 — a 5.5-liter flat-plane V8 and the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever put in a production car.
parts.detail: 670 hp at 8,400 rpm to an 8,600 rpm redline, hand-built at Bowling Green. DOHC 32-valve with a dry-sump oiling system, an active split intake on twin 87 mm throttle bodies, and forged titanium rods.
parts.watch: Early 2023 builds have a known front timing-cover oil leak (backordered one-time-use bolts) and a few warranty engine replacements — buy sorted, keep the warranty, and run dexos-R 5W-50.

parts.label: Forged / Carbon-Fiber Wheels
parts.summary: Wide staggered wheels — with the Z07 option, one-piece carbon-fiber rims that slash unsprung mass.
parts.detail: Staggered forged wheels put 670 hp and the Z07 aero down; the optional carbon-fiber wheels shave serious unsprung weight for sharper response.
parts.watch: The carbon wheels on run-flats are notoriously hard to service — many dealers can't seat the tires. Aftermarket wheels are a popular escape.

parts.label: Brembo Carbon-Ceramic Brakes
parts.summary: Big Brembo brakes with available carbon-ceramic rotors (Z07) for repeated high-speed stops with minimal fade.
parts.detail: Brembo calipers on huge rotors — carbon-ceramics with the Z07 package — haul a ~3,600 lb car down from supercar speed lap after lap.
parts.watch: Carbon-ceramics are exotic-car expensive to replace, and the carbon wheels make tire and brake service harder.

parts.label: Two-Seat Cockpit
parts.summary: A driver-wrapped two-seat cockpit — the C8's tall center console and square-rim wheel.
parts.detail: Two seats behind a wide digital cluster; the Z06 layers in carbon-fiber and microsuede trim. The square-rimmed wheel keeps the reconfigurable dash in clear view.
parts.watch: Early infotainment quirks and trim rattles on some cars; check the seat bolsters on hard-used examples.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: Full-LED lighting — slim C8 headlamps and the signature quad taillamps.
parts.detail: Slim LED headlights up front and the C8's four-lamp tail signature, plus the drive-mode electronics and the Z06's active-valve exhaust controls.
parts.watch: Aging lighting and control modules can be costly to replace as a unit; watch for early-build software gremlins.

parts.label: Body, Aero & Glass
parts.summary: A mid-engine composite-and-aluminum body 3.6 inches wider than the Stingray, with Z07 aero making real downforce.
parts.detail: Wider track and bodywork than the Stingray, with an available carbon aero package — front splitter and a big rear wing — that generates genuine downforce at speed.
parts.watch: Front-end and splitter stone chips; carbon parts are costly, and early cars saw carbon-fiber supply delays.

parts.label: 8-Speed DCT Transaxle
parts.summary: An 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle mounted behind the mid-engine V8, driving the rear wheels.
parts.detail: 8-speed Tremec TR-9080 dual-clutch transaxle behind the mid-mounted V8, spinning the rears through a short 5.56 final drive — 0–60 in about 2.6 seconds with Z07. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — the transaxle isn't a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Some cars show dual-clutch gasket leaks and transient error messages; service the transaxle fluid on schedule.

parts.label: Magnetic Ride 4.0 Suspension
parts.summary: Magnetic Ride Control 4.0 on a track 3.6 inches wider than the Stingray; the Z07 adds stiffer springs and aggressive aero.
parts.detail: Adaptive magnetorheological dampers on a much wider track than the Stingray. The Z07 package stiffens the springs, adds carbon-ceramics, and makes real aero downforce. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — the suspension isn't a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Z07 cars ride firm and wear pads and tires quickly on track; alignment is fussy after any suspension work.
